centered-guides.json.title: Genmitsu 3018-PROVer V2 retrofit
centered-guides.json.target: Replace the integrated Genmitsu motion board with Prime P12 direct motor-phase outputs. Use the depicted separate Cytron spindle stage and qualified interfaces for probe, limits, optional laser, pump, emergency stop and unsupported factory UI.
centered-guides.json.plan: Original motion-driver electronics are on the board being replaced. Use Prime integrated phase outputs directly to measured winding pairs; do not connect STEP/DIR signal outputs to motor windings. Confirm installed board, motor current and power rating from the cited machine source. Selected architecture: Prime P12 with integrated motor drivers. The main diagram and connection-ID schedule define the current proposed routes. Dotted function-coloured GUESS routes need the named commissioning checks; OPEN routes remain disconnected until the missing terminal, rating or interface is established. Previous Core alternatives remain only in the superseded historical architecture record.

775 spindle controller: PWM, direction and motor output

Smoothie PWM candidate (verify board) · J35.6 TIM1_CH1 (PWM candidate) → Cytron MD10C R3.0 · PWM (spindle speed PWM candidate); Smoothie PWM candidate (verify board) · J35.10 GND → Cytron MD10C R3.0 · GND (control signal reference); Cytron MD10C R3.0 · OUT A → 775 spindle: measured motor terminals (polarity unknown) · measured motor terminal 1 (switched motor output A); Cytron MD10C R3.0 · OUT B → 775 spindle: measured motor terminals (polarity unknown) · measured motor terminal 2 (switched motor output B); Smoothie PWM candidate (verify board) · logic GND (fixed DIR candidate) → Cytron MD10C R3.0 · DIR (fixed direction logic low candidate)
GUESS

Prime J35.6 exports TIM1_CH1 (PWM candidate) and J35.10 GND. Cytron MD10C R3.0 has PWM, DIR, GND, VM, PWR_GND, OUT_A/B; manual Rev3.0 V1.0 Aug 2018 supports sign-magnitude PWM+DIR and 3.3/5V logic. DIR tied to logic GND selects Forward while PWM is high per the manual truth table; bench-check actual spindle rotation and ensure PWM low stops/brakes as expected. Separate motor supply must match measured motor voltage/current and be fused. Do not use guessed red/black wiring. Resource conflict: spindle PWM C04-001 and optional laser PWM C14-001 both nominate Prime J35.6 TIM1_CH1. These are mutually exclusive alternatives, not two independent outputs. Disconnect the unused load or source and configure a distinct supported PWM output; never wire both loads expecting independent control.

Prime selected · separate logic and motor supplies

Regulated 5 V logic supply · +5 V regulated → Prime P12 · confirm exact revision · J42.1 · 5V_PORTIN (Prime regulated logic supply); Regulated 5 V logic supply · 0 V logic return → Prime P12 · confirm exact revision · J42.2 · GND (Prime logic supply return); Verified motor supply · voltage/current TBD · DC + · before fuse → Motor branch fuse · rating selected after measurement · fuse input (Protected motor branch input); Motor branch fuse · rating selected after measurement · fuse output → Prime P12 · confirm exact revision · J9.1 · VMOT (Prime VMOT power); Verified motor supply · voltage/current TBD · 0 V motor return → Prime P12 · confirm exact revision · J9.2 · GND (Prime motor supply return)
GUESS

This is the selected Prime P12 integrated-driver architecture. Use the current P12 PCB-derived contact labels; other board revisions require their own verified pinout and driver ratings. Use one verified power-entry arrangement; J10 parallels VMOT and is left unused here. Board ground is shared internally; route motor current directly to power distribution, not through logic wiring. Determine actual allowed voltage/current before choosing a supply; no machine-source adapter automatically qualifies.

Prime P12 · dedicated PROBE J31 · J31.4 · conditioned PROBE signal → Measured passive Z plate + tool clip · Plate lead · continuity identify (Probe plate signal); Prime P12 · dedicated PROBE J31 · J31.3 · GND → Measured passive Z plate + tool clip · Tool clip return · continuity identify (Separate probe return)
GUESS

Documented probe kit; verify this fitted kit is a passive isolated contact. J31.4 is conditioned through comparator U24; establish JP7/JP8 population and safe pull-up/configuration from the exact P12 sheet. Leave J31.1 VMOT and J31.2 selected supply unused for a passive plate. Probe input maximum differs between board guides; no high-voltage capability is claimed.

Prime J35.6 is only a proposed PWM resource; verify firmware ownership. Resource conflict: spindle PWM C04-001 and optional laser PWM C14-001 both nominate Prime J35.6 TIM1_CH1. These are mutually exclusive alternatives, not two independent outputs. Disconnect the unused load or source and configure a distinct supported PWM output; never wire both loads expecting independent control.
Air pump interface · optional/fitted pump must be identified

Prime P12 · conditional pump power stage · J20.1 · cutoff-switched VFET → Pump branch fuse · rating after load measurement · Fuse input (Switched rail into pump branch fuse); Pump branch fuse · rating after load measurement · Fuse output → Identified DC air pump · fitted status/rating unknown · Measured pump + (Fused pump supply); Identified DC air pump · fitted status/rating unknown · Measured pump − → Prime P12 · conditional pump power stage · J20.2 · Q22 switched return (Pump low-side switched return)
GUESS

Manual pp.19–20 names the air-pump interface but gives no pump model, connector pin map or load rating. Proposed DC pump load on Fan2 only after VFET voltage, startup/stall current, flyback suppression and connector rating are established. J20.1 is cutoff-switched VFET, J20.2 Q22 switched return; verify exact P12 firmware/resource assignment and reuse one VFET supply, not a second source tied to the same rail.
Emergency stop · independent hazardous-energy interruption

Fitted E-stop switch · contacts must be traced · Identify stop-chain contact A → Independent hardware stop chain · retain or engineer · Identify monitored stop-loop input (Hardwired stop chain input); Fitted E-stop switch · contacts must be traced · Identify stop-chain contact B → Independent hardware stop chain · retain or engineer · Identify stop-loop return (Hardwired stop chain return)
OPEN

Manual pp.19–20 names E-stop interface without contact numbers or safety topology. Trace fitted switch and contactor/drive-inhibit circuit before wiring. Board-only firmware stop cannot assure safe stop. No Prime GPIO is presented as the hazardous-energy cut-off.
Factory offline controller and MPG · protocol is not a GPIO pinout

Prime P12 · no validated factory pendant interface · Compatible host interface · unsupported factory protocol → Factory offline controller · optional accessory · Factory-only interface · connector unspecified (Factory offline interface compatibility); Prime P12 · no validated factory pendant interface · Compatible host interface · unsupported factory protocol → Factory MPG/handwheel interface · fitted status unresolved · MPG interface · protocol unspecified (Factory MPG interface compatibility)
OPEN

Manual p.28 warns factory offline port is designed for its controller and must not connect other controllers. Keep factory offline controller/MPG disconnected from Prime until protocol, electrical levels and replacement firmware support are established. J30 debug UART is not an assumed factory pendant adapter.

pins: Genmitsu factory motor outputs are TB67S109-driven phases; they must not connect to Core STEP/DIR. For Prime candidate X/Y/Z J5/J6/J7 phase output contacts are pin1 B2, pin2 B1, pin3 A2, pin4 A1; individual machine lead-to-coil assignment remains test-gated.

Core external driver signal tuples: X J5.16 STEP_A -> SN74LVC07A pin1 A1/pin2 Y1 -> DM320T P1 PUL; J5.18 DIR_A -> pin3 A2/pin4 Y2 -> P1 DIR; J5.20 GND -> pin7; J5.10 3V3 -> pin14 VCC. Y: J5.22/.24/.26 -> chip pins5/6 and 9/8; Z: J5.28/.30/.32 -> pins11/10 and 13/12. P1 OPTO is regulated +5V; P2 +Vdc/GND is motor supply; P2 A+/A-/B+/B- connect to measured coils.

Spindle peripheral: Cytron MD10C control terminals PWM, DIR, GND; stage terminals VM/GND and OUT A/B. Candidate Smoothie PWM J35.6 TIM1_CH1 and reference J35.10 GND need board/header/firmware verification. Machine spindle red/black leads are documented polarity, but actual mating cavity mapping remains unknown.
Smoothieboard V2 Core P1 J42 candidate supply inlet: pin1=/5VPORTIN, pin2=GND (exported board contacts). Verify exact board-revision supply specifications before connection; pin1 is not a 5V output.
parts: One StepperOnline DM320T per Core-controlled axis, with a TI SN74LVC07A six-channel open-drain buffer proposal (three buffers, one per axis (only two of six channels loaded per device)); manual exposes P1 PUL/DIR/OPTO/ENA and P2 +Vdc/GND/A+/A-/B+/B-.

Cytron MD10C R3.0 candidate for the brushed 775 spindle; dedicated fused supply after measuring motor current. R3.0 manual supports PWM+DIR sign-magnitude with 3.3/5V logic; fixed DIR logic must be verified before tying.
Retain the physical E-stop/safety chain; identify machine switch/probe/laser peripherals before wiring.
instructions: Core power candidate: route the selected, fused and voltage-verified board supply to Core P1 J42.1 (/5VPORTIN) and supply return to J42.2 (GND). Check exact Core revision input range/current and upstream fuse before energizing; do not mistake J42.1 for a 5V output.
Record board/motor/PSU revision and use continuity to identify each 4-wire motor coil pair before connection.

For Core, use SN74LVC07A channels as 3.3V-input open-drain sinks: for each axis use one SN74LVC07A (STEP A1→Y1 pins1→2, DIR A2→Y2 pins3→4); pins5/6,9/8,11/10,13/12 remain unused. Power each pin14 from Core J5.10 3V3, pin7 to one verified J5 return, and fit 100nF directly across each device. DM320T PUL/DIR inputs draw 7–16mA each: two loaded sinks total 14–32mA/device, below TI 100mA package GND-current absolute maximum; verify actual input-current setting and scope pulse timing.
Set motor current from the motor nameplate, fuse every stage, and test one unloaded axis at conservative speed.
Map each individual MIN and MAX switch to its own Prime input only after continuity and NO/NC checks; do not infer connector assignment from socket placement.
Test PWM into MD10C with spindle disconnected first; then test secured spindle at low duty/current. Prove E-stop removes hazardous energy independent of firmware.
